### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **5** package(s): `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/plugin-email`, `@objectstack/plugin-webhooks`, `@objectstack/service-settings`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **18** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **7** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/platform-objects/src/audit/sys-identity-email.object.ts`, `packages/platform-objects/src/system/sys-platform-setting-audit.object.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/email-log-objects.ts`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**5** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/webhooks.mdx`  _(via AutoEnqueuer (symbol, a top-level class), SysWebhook (symbol, a top-level const object), managed_by (literal, a string literal in holders))_
- `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`  _(via managed_by (literal, a string literal in holders))_
- `content/docs/permissions/authorization.mdx`  _(via managed_by (literal, a string literal in holders))_
- `content/docs/permissions/permission-sets.mdx`  _(via managed_by (literal, a string literal in holders))_
- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via sys_setting_audit (symbol, a field of const object enObjects; a field of const object esESObjects; a field of const object jaJPObjects; a field of const object zhCNObjects))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v12.mdx`  _(via managed_by (literal, a string literal in holders))_
- `content/docs/releases/v15.mdx`  _(via managed_by (literal, a string literal in holders))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **7** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/platform-objects/src/audit/sys-identity-email.object.ts`, `packages/platform-objects/src/system/sys-platform-setting-audit.object.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/email-log-objects.ts`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **146** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1366740c6c80be43b18b6b72a68736032245e3e9` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `3c303f2f23b47d92a8fe7423343f7f7b8f18e5d0` — the merge of head `cdd16215002a2e9450296f0342eba95261a463d5` into base `1366740c6c80be43b18b6b72a68736032245e3e9`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 3c303f2f23b47d92a8fe7423343f7f7b8f18e5d0 && git checkout 3c303f2f23b47d92a8fe7423343f7f7b8f18e5d0
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 1366740c6c80be43b18b6b72a68736032245e3e9 cdd16215002a2e9450296f0342eba95261a463d5 && git checkout -B drift-repro 1366740c6c80be43b18b6b72a68736032245e3e9 && git merge --no-ff cdd16215002a2e9450296f0342eba95261a463d5

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1366740c6c80be43b18b6b72a68736032245e3e9
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 1366740c6c80be43b18b6b72a68736032245e3e9` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `8f6bf26e61f0f3d2a49359d17b3d10d4f663b6a7`
Local-runs: none

PR #24836 · card #24583, step 7 part 7c · merge-base `ddb3360a4954c1ccb6878deb3ca0b303c79d3289` · 26 files, +252/−291 · face: declaration (`Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` on the PR body and in `.changeset/24583-7c-dual-reads-retired.md`). Read: the diff, the dev report (6287753302), the claim (6284522037), the step-1 settlement notes (6271949316 on #24581), ADR-0131 D2/D6/D7/D10, the ceremony on main (`packages/cli/src/utils/organization-ownership-apply.ts`, landed by #24681 at `12d14765c`), and the head's check-runs. Nothing built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

**1. Webhooks — the dual read is gone; what remains is regime C, and it is pinned.**

- Deleted, confirmed against main: `classifyDeclaredNameHolder` (main `declared-webhooks.ts:264`; no definition at head — the only surviving mention in the tree is liveness-ledger prose, residual R2); `AutoEnqueuer.resolveDeclared`'s `mirrorIds` and the `continue` skip (main `auto-enqueuer.ts:475`, `:564-567`, `:586`); the redeliver guard's mirror branch (main `redeliver-guard.ts:143-146`) and `judgeDeclared`'s `known` parameter. At head the holder read asks `fields: ['id', 'name']` (`auto-enqueuer.ts:547`), every holder lands in `heldByRow` (`:560`), and the declaration is withheld and said once per name by `reportDeclarationWithheld` (`:614-618`).
- Can a pristine mirror still exist after the ceremony? On a certified database, no. `runDeclaredWebhooks` (`organization-ownership-apply.ts:3178`) selects every `managed_by` package/platform row (`:3187-3188`); for each name a package declares it deletes a pristine or switch-only copy after re-sourcing its deliveries to `declared:NAME` (`:3256-3262`, the `resource` closure ≈`:3225-3240` throws if any delivery still names the row), or clones an edited copy under a free name with `managed_by 'admin'` and `customized` false (`:3264-3286`); a customized copy under a wall blocks the step (`:3209-3218`), so that database is not certified. On a fresh install there was never a seeder: `bootstrapDeclaredWebhooks` has no definition in the tree, and no live code writes `managed_by: 'package'` or `'platform'` into `sys_webhook`. The one survivor is the 5a leftover — a seeded row whose name no installed package declares (`:3201-3208`, kept and reported). If a package later declares that name, the row now withholds the declaration instead of being skipped. That is regime C (ADR-0131 D6: same-name shadowing is retired, a declaration arriving over an existing row is reported and never becomes an overlay; the remedies are rename or delete the row, or clone plus the `sys_metadata_activation` switch), and `declared-webhooks.ts:59-76` records exactly that. Pinned: `declared-webhooks.test.ts:470` ("a seeded row the ceremony left, its name declared later, withholds the declaration: one delivery, from the row" — one call with `refId: 'whk_left'` at the row's URL, not the declaration's `task-v2`; one warn; no writes) and `:492` (row `active: false`, ledger `true`: nothing fires — the row governs, not the ledger).
- Deliveries whose `ref_id` is a mirror row id: on a certified database 5a re-sourced them before the delete, and the step refuses to delete while one remains. A delivery naming a clone keeps the clone's id, and the clone row exists; one naming a 5a leftover names a live row. The guard judges each by the row: `redeliver-guard.ts:123` (declared refs go to `judgeDeclared`), `:126-130` (row read), `:132` (row gone → refused, fail-closed), `:147` (inactive → refused). No misjudgement. Pinned at `declared-webhooks.test.ts:590` (a pristine holder under a switched-off declaration: replay allowed, by the row) and `:600`.

**2. Kept on measurement — both right, both complete-feature-safe.**

- `bindWebhookProvenanceStamp` (`webhook-provenance.ts:70`; bound at `webhook-outbox-plugin.ts:330`). The claim's condition, "once nothing reads `customized`", does not hold. The ceremony reads it at `organization-ownership-apply.ts:3188` (the select), `:3209` (the wall blocker) and `:3256-3257` (delete vs activation row vs clone), and the apply "starts over (each step is idempotent)" when the reviewed plan's inventory digest supersedes the recorded checkpoint (`:205-207`; `restartedFrom` at `:596` and `:4138`). Without the stamp, an administrator's edit of a 5a leftover whose name a package declares later would read as pristine on that re-run and be deleted. Keeping it is correct; its docblock names that reader (`webhook-provenance.ts:6-15`), and the stamp stays pinned (`declared-webhooks.test.ts:526`; `webhook-provenance.per-row.test.ts`, unchanged).
- `migrateLegacyWebhookSecrets` (`migrate-webhook-secrets.ts:87`): docblock only — the file's 23 changed lines all sit in the header comment (`:8-27`); no code line moves. The narrowing in prose is correct and complete for the code: authored rows, the ceremony's clones (which keep `definition_json`, `:3273`) and undeclared seeded rows can each still carry a cleartext blob, and the sweep is keyed on data, so a provenance filter would skip rows that still hold a key. Complete-feature-safe: on a fresh install the sweep finds nothing and is idempotent; nothing it reads was removed.

**3. Settings audit — `global` retired from `sys_setting_audit.scope`, declared as a narrowing.**

- Writers. `buildSettingAuditWriter` routes by `settingAuditObjectFor` (`settings-service-plugin.ts:572-573`, `:618`): a global entry inserts into `sys_platform_setting_audit` (`:651`); the `sys_setting_audit` insert is the non-global branch only (`:655`). `config-change-audit.ts` writes `sys_audit_log` (`:300`), never this table. No other writer in `packages/`, `apps/`, `examples/` or `scripts/`. The only `scope = 'global'` rows in the tree are the 18.0 fixture's (`packages/qa/dogfood/test/upgrade-harness/fixture-18.0/database.sql:660`, `:662`), which 5b moves: `SIBLING_MOVES` `global-audit-move` selects by scope, never by NULL (`organization-ownership-apply.ts:3353-3359`), as the step-2 settlement note required, and the harness pins `COUNT(*) WHERE scope = 'global'` = 0 on the certified file (`upgrade-18x-harness.dogfood.test.ts:248`). So after 5b no `global` row remains on a certified database, and the v18 boot guard refuses an uncertified one.
- A stored `global` row, were one to exist: nothing on read. Select options are validated in the record validator (`record-validator.ts:55-57`), which the write paths call (`engine.ts:17827`, `:18172`); no read path validates, so the row reads back as stored and shows as a select-option miss (its translation leaves are gone). `keptOptionValues` is the import's exception (#22183), not a reader's. A later update of such a row would be refused on `scope` — moot for an append-only ledger. A new insert is refused `VALIDATION_FAILED` on `scope`, pinned twice: `settings-deployment-level-expand.test.ts:217` (refused before the driver; the writer's global row lands in the sibling; control at `:211`) and the dogfood `settings-audit-global-rung-sibling.dogfood.test.ts:134` (booted again over the same file, through the system context; control at `:127`).
- Declaration. The changeset carries `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, the `**BREAKING**` banner and one ADR-0087 marker, `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, with its reasons (no spec key, export, type or error code removed; a stored select value refused on one platform object; both narrowings reach only rows the ceremony settles before certification). AGENTS.md §3 (`:1087-1101`): `(narrowing)` is BREAKING, `yes` takes at least `minor`, exactly one marker — met; `Check Changeset` is green on this head. Spec liveness needs nothing: `sys_setting_audit.scope` is a platform-object field, not a `packages/spec` property, no ledger row names it, and `Spec property liveness` is green. The four translation bundles (en, es-ES, ja-JP, zh-CN) each drop the `global` leaf, the es-ES source hash for it is gone, and the echo ledger steps 45→44 with its decision line removed (`objects-es-es-echo-decisions.test.ts:245-248`).

**4. Identity mail — docblocks only.** `sys-email.object.ts:100-111` (comment lines inside the gate's rationale), `sys-identity-email.object.ts:22-25`, `email-log-objects.ts:15-21`, `email-plugin.ts:1000-1002` (a comment above the unchanged sweep). No executable line changes in plugin-email or in the two platform-objects mail objects; the body read gate and the no-object mail job's `sys_email` read stand, as the claim said nothing was removable.

**5. The two object files in the diff.** `sys-webhook.object.ts`: two docblock hunks — the header's account of the 18.0 rows (`:20-24`, now regime C) and the `managed_by` field comment (`:275-277`: `customized` is the ceremony's record, no longer the dispatcher's switch). Why: both described the dual read this PR retires; the field list, options and gates are untouched (`managed_by: Field.select(` at `:278`). `sys-platform-setting-audit.object.ts`: two docblock hunks — "one reader reads both tables" → "either table … never `global` there" (`:15-16`), and "a reader of the global rung's history reads both" → "this table alone" (`:30-33`). Why: the claim's "history reads both tables" docblock fix. `scope` stays `['global']` (`:86-87`), pinned at `sys-setting.scope-options.test.ts:64`.

**6. Tests — rewritten to the new rule; nothing weakened.** `declared-webhooks.test.ts` §3: the four old mirror-skip pins are replaced by their inverses (`:470`, `:492`, `:590`); "customized, switched off, said once" folds into `:470` and `:492`, since `customized` no longer participates in dispatch; the stamp pin (`:526`) keeps the `customized: true` assertion and drops its dispatch half, which the rule no longer owns. `:508`, `:534`, `:552`, `:600` are unchanged in substance. `sys-setting.scope-options.test.ts:64` now pins the split both ways (audit table = spec enum minus `global`; sibling = `['global']`). The expand test and the dogfood test each replace the dual-read case with a refusal plus a tenant-rung control. The ablation (dev-reported, not re-run here): the mirror skip restored in `resolveDeclared` reds `:470` and `:492` — the two regime-C pins — and nothing else, which matches the rule's surface.

**7. Check-runs on `8f6bf26e6`** (polled 09:32Z): 26 success, 7 skipped, 7 in progress — Test Core 1/6 to 6/6 and Type Check · workspace. No failure. The dogfood shard matrix is skipped for this PR's paths; the dogfood rewrites rest on the dev's reported 50/50 run.

### ② Semver level

`minor` on `@objectstack/plugin-webhooks` and `@objectstack/platform-objects`, with the `!` title and the `**BREAKING**` banner: a run-time narrowing (a pristine seeded holder no longer yields to its declaration; a stored select value refused on one platform object), with no spec key, export, type or error code removed. This is the repo's pre-GA rule — ADR-0087 "Ratified: the pre-launch launch-window exemption", amended 2026-09-13 (#18003): a metadata-facing break ships `minor`, carrying the banner and its ADR-0087 disposition — and the same wording as the precedents in plugin-webhooks `18.0.0-next.1` and platform-objects `18.0.0-next.3`. Level correct. `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` is the right line: measured (R1–R4, the harness, four suites) and a narrowing.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Governed paths: none (0/26; `Governed Surface Queue Guard` green). ⛔ Not the ceremony files of #24681 and ⛔ not `docs/adr/**` — both held.
- Base discipline: branched from main merged with the ceremony branch under 6270035914; #24681 landed (`12d14765c`), main merged again (`78f99c34c`), and the deferred `migration.mdx` regeneration is discharged at the head, equal to main.
- Residuals, none blocking:
  - R1 `packages/platform-objects/src/system/sys-setting.object.ts:133-135` still says the sibling audit object "keeps all three, because the audit writer records a global-scope change too" — false after this PR. Fix: one line, "keeps `tenant` and `user`; the global rung's audit row lives in `sys_platform_setting_audit`".
  - R2 `packages/spec/liveness/webhook.json`, `props.name.evidence` (verifiedAt 2026-10-19), reads "`classifyDeclaredNameHolder` decides which answers" — a deleted symbol, in prose the liveness gate does not resolve (it checks `path#symbol` anchors; `auto-enqueuer.ts#resolveDeclared` still exists, so the anchor holds). Fix: amend the parenthetical to "the row holding it answers and the declaration is withheld (regime C)". Outside the claim's file surface, so no breach.
  - R3 `.changeset/24529-declared-webhooks-from-registry.md:25` (step 1, unreleased) still teaches the mirror skip; it and this changeset ship in one CHANGELOG. A one-line "superseded in 7c" note would spare the docs sweep a hit. Not 7c's file.
  - R4 The changeset attributes the launch-window convention to "ADR-0131 D2, D6, D7"; those decisions motivate the change, while the convention is ADR-0087's section named above. Wording only.
  - R5 Dev-reported deviation: commit `174abe92a` carries a trailer naming a model; later commits do not, and history on the shared branch was not rewritten. A squash on landing resolves it.

**Head `cdd162150`.** The review PASSED at `8f6bf26e6` (6287997289). Since then the branch has taken one clean merge of `main` (`1366740c6`) and one text-only commit for the review's R1–R4.

**Deliberate correction (#17712).** `.changeset/24529-declared-webhooks-from-registry.md` is an unreleased note from another PR. Its two 18.0-database bullets taught the mirror skip that this PR retires. They are corrected in place, not restored: the ceremony deletes the pristine copy and re-points its deliveries at `declared:NAME`, and the boot guard refuses until certification. Check Changeset is red on that file by design; it is not a required check. The seat batches this correction, with any others step 7 makes, into one confirmation card for the maintainer.

Not governed; 556 changed lines. The seat marks it ready and arms auto-merge.
